blurb: Anglo-Scottish sheepdog prized for herding skill, stamina and trainability
description: The Border Collie is a medium-sized British herding dog from the Anglo-Scottish border, with a double coat in many colors and a reputation for intelligence.
answer: The Border Collie is a medium-sized British herding dog of collie type from the region of the Anglo-Scottish border, descended from traditional British sheepdogs. Males stand 48 to 56 cm and females 46 to 53 cm. It is kept mainly for herding or as a companion, and some claim it is the most intelligent breed of dog.

body: The breed descends from landrace collies found widely in the British Isles, and its name reflects its probable origin along the Anglo-Scottish border. All purebred Border Collies alive today trace back to Old Hemp, a tricolor dog born in Northumberland in 1893 whose quiet, powerful working style became the Border Collie style.

The term border collie was first used in 1915 by James Reid of the International Sheep Dog Society to distinguish working dogs from the Kennel Club's show collies. Dogs were exported to New Zealand and Australia from the 1890s, and the American Kennel Club recognized the breed in 1995, against protests from working-dog groups.

Border Collies are medium-sized with a moderate double coat that ranges from smooth to rough and is often thick and prone to shedding. Black and white is most common, but almost any color appears, including tricolor, liver and white, merle and Australian red. Eyes range from brown to green, and ears may be erect, dropped or semi-erect. Working registries judge dogs by ability rather than looks, while show standards ask for a keen, intelligent expression.

The breed is commonly described as highly intelligent, driven and very trainable, and working dogs take direction by voice and whistle at long distances. Research dogs such as Chaser, said to know over a thousand words, are often cited for its learning ability. Sources focus on working traits and give little other detail on temperament.

Bred for work, the Border Collie has notable energy, speed and stamina, and is one of the most popular breeds for agility, flyball, obedience, disc dog and tracking. It is still used to herd sheep, cattle and other livestock, and in mountain rescue in Britain. The thick coat is noted as prone to shedding.

A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.1 years. Conditions reported in the breed include collie eye anomaly, congenital and adult-onset deafness, neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis, trapped neutrophil syndrome, Border Collie collapse, liver tumors and the MDR1 mutation, which makes some common drugs riskier. DNA tests exist for several of these conditions.

faq.q: Is the Border Collie the smartest dog breed?
faq.a: Some have claimed it is the most intelligent breed, and individual dogs such as Chaser and Rico have been studied for learning hundreds of words. Intelligence rankings depend on how they are measured.

faq.q: How big does a Border Collie get?
faq.a: Males stand 48 to 56 cm at the withers and females 46 to 53 cm. It is a medium-sized breed.

faq.q: How long do Border Collies live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.1 years, and a 2022 English study found 12.1 years.
Yes. Their double coat is often thick and prone to shedding, whether smooth or rough.
